# isomesh — BACKLOG ARCHIVE

Completed tickets, moved here from `BACKLOG.md` as they finished. **Never deleted.**

The annotations matter more than the checkmarks: several of these tickets were amended, split or
outright contradicted during implementation, and the reason is recorded on the row rather than lost to
the commit log. Where a ticket's premise turned out to be false, `FINDINGS.md` carries the falsified
entry and this file carries what the ticket did about it.

**Archived:** continuously since 2026-08-11. Rows are in completion order, not numeric order.

## Index

312 tickets. Line numbers are stable until something above them is edited — grep the ID if
they drift. **Read the annotation, not the checkmark**: the rows worth revisiting are the ones where
implementation contradicted the ticket.

| | | *Scope added, deliberately.* **(a)** A `ReferenceField` trait (`NAME`, `domain`, `closed_in_domain`, `expected_euler`, `is_exact_distance`). Without it the harness needs a per-field `if` ladder, because `gyroid` is periodic (a finite box cuts it, so it has boundary) and `fbm_terrain` is a heightfield (open by construction) — neither has an Euler characteristic assertable a priori, and inventing one would violate rule 5. **(b)** The canonical gyroid is capped to a sphere so it is closed at all, which needs an `Intersection` combinator alongside `Difference`. **(c)** `for_each_reference_field!` sweeps all seven with concrete types; `Vec<Box<dyn Sdf>>` would put a vtable on the innermost loop of every benchmark. | | |
| | | *Two numbers worth recording.* No document in this repo contains a single field formula, so all seven originate here, each cited in its doc comment. `fbm_terrain`'s noise is hand-rolled (rule 3 forbids a noise crate) and evaluates **no transcendental at all** — integer hash plus a polynomial — so it is bit-identical across platforms, which is what T-007's committed goldens need. Its amplitude bound is the **provable** `\|n\| ≤ 2` rather than the widely quoted `√3/2 ≈ 0.866`; measured max is **0.907716** over 43,200 samples, i.e. the folklore figure is *wrong for this implementation* and hard-coding it would have been a silent bug. | | |
| ☑ | **T-001** | **Mesh validity harness** — `crates/isomesh/src/validate.rs`, compiled in normal builds (consumers want it too). Reports, doesn't just assert: `euler_characteristic`, `non_manifold_edges` (edge used by ≠2 faces), `non_manifold_vertices`, `boundary_edges`, `degenerate_triangles`, `out_of_range_indices`, `duplicate_vertices`. Returns a `MeshReport` struct that `Display`s as one block. **Acceptance:** unit-tested against a hand-built tetrahedron (χ=2, 0 violations) and a deliberately broken mesh (each violation type detected). | M | I-002 |
| | | *Definitional choices, each a judgment call rather than a fact.* **(a)** `non_manifold_edges` counts ≥3 faces and `boundary_edges` exactly 1, splitting the ticket's literal "≠2" — lumping them together double-counts and makes zero unachievable for any open mesh, i.e. for `fbm_terrain` and for every individual chunk. **(b)** `V` in χ is *referenced* vertices, with `unreferenced_vertices` reported separately; otherwise a stale vertex pool reports χ=3 for a sphere and reads as a topology bug when it's an allocation bug. **(c)** `duplicate_vertices` is "has an earlier vertex within ε" — epsilon-closeness isn't transitive, so equivalence classes aren't well defined but this is. **(d)** `genus` is `Some` only for a single, consistently oriented, manifold component with no skipped faces; the orientation precondition is what makes `χ = 2−2g−b` sound. **(e)** No `Result`, no panic, no short-circuit: a `Result` forces a branch at every call site and `?` discards the partial report exactly when it's most useful. | | |
| | | *Three counters added beyond the list, each because its absence is a hole.* `inconsistently_oriented_edges` — a case table with one flipped triangle passes χ, edge-manifoldness *and* vertex-manifoldness while being inside out (fixture 10 demonstrates it). `boundary_loops` — `χ=1` alone can't distinguish a hole from a handle, and it's `b` not the edge count that enters `χ = 2−2g−b`. `non_finite_positions` — a NaN vertex quantises into one bucket, never matches as a duplicate, and `NaN <= threshold` is false so it isn't degenerate either; without this it passes silently. Also: `degenerate_triangles` is excluded from `violations()` and is a recorded metric, since Marching Cubes emits slivers for ordinary reasons. | | |
| ☑ | **T-002** | **Self-intersection counter.** Triangle–triangle intersection test, BVH or uniform grid broadphase. Reports intersections per 1,000 triangles. Doesn't need to be fast; needs to be right. **Acceptance:** two hand-placed crossing triangles detected; two adjacent triangles sharing an edge **not** counted (this is the trap). | M | T-001 |
| | | *Returns the intersecting **pairs**, not just a count.* The literature review is explicit that every detected pair must be bucketed intra-cell / inter-cell-within-chunk / cross-chunk-seam, since cross-seam hits are a stitching bug that would otherwise dominate λ. Chunks don't exist until G-001, so rather than invent a chunk concept now, the pairs come back sorted and bucketing becomes a caller's job the moment there's something to bucket by. Reports λ (per 1,000 triangles), never `p` — `p = 1 − e^{−λT}` saturates with chunk size. | | |
| | | *Two judgment calls.* **(a)** Pairs sharing **any** vertex index are excluded, not just edge-sharing ones. The ticket names the edge case, but excluding only that would report a false positive for every non-consecutive pair in every vertex fan, which swamps λ. Documented cost: a fold pinching exactly at a shared vertex isn't counted. **(b)** Tangential contact — meeting along a line or at a point — doesn't count; only overlap of positive measure does. Otherwise every correctly-stitched neighbour reads as a defect. Coplanar overlap *is* counted, via a separate 2D separating-axis path. | | |
| ☑ | **T-004** | **Determinism harness.** Run any extractor twice, assert byte-identical output buffers. **Acceptance:** wired into the test suite as a helper that every algorithm ticket calls. Catches `HashMap` iteration order leaking into vertex order — which it will. | S | T-001 |
| | | *"Byte-identical" is not `==`, and `==` is wrong in **both** directions:* `+0.0 == -0.0` is true though the bits differ (a sign flip on a zero coordinate is exactly what a reordered summation produces), and `NaN != NaN` is true though the bits may match. Comparison goes through `Real::total_cmp`, the IEEE `totalOrder` predicate, which compares full bit patterns. One fixture per direction. | | |
| | | *Three runs, not two.* Two fresh buffers catch non-determinism in the extractor; a third run into a **reused** buffer catches output that depends on the buffer's prior state. Every algorithm here is meant to be driven by resetting one buffer across thousands of chunks (rule 6) and nothing else in the suite drives one that way. | | |

What is buildable now is everything that does not need an extractor, and it is built. **Randomized fields have no known surface**, so the property checked is that they are **1-Lipschitz** (`min`/`max` of 1-Lipschitz functions are), which holds *everywhere* including the seams where a gradient check would have to skip. Negative controls: a field scaled by two must violate Lipschitz; a non-manifold mesh and a bad index must each stop the bundle. | | |

| ☑ | **A-001** | **Marching Cubes.** Standard 256-case table. **Also write the structural validator** described in the brief: for all 256 configurations, generated triangles' boundary edges must lie on cube faces and be consistent with that face's corner signs. Cite the table's source in a comment. Document the sign convention (**negative = inside**) and winding order on the public fn. | L | T-001, T-005a |
| | | *The table is **derived at compile time**, not transcribed.* home-still holds the right papers — Lewiner et al. 2003 (`10.1080/10867651.2003.10487582`) and Lengyel's 2010 dissertation — but **their case tables did not survive PDF→text conversion**: Lengyel's are figures of cube diagrams, Lewiner's Table 1 converts to scrambled cells. Reading triangulations off diagrams is the guessing rule 5 forbids. So the construction walks each face's corners CCW-from-outside; every cut edge gets exactly one entry and one exit (two faces induce opposite directions on a shared edge), the segments close into directed cycles with nothing left over, and each cycle is fanned. Lengyel §3.1.1 supplies the structure, the sign convention and the zero-sample rule — cited, and quoted in the module docs. | | |
| | | *Cross-checked against the published table anyway.* Bourke's listing was fetched with `curl` and parsed by regex — no language model ever touched a digit — and is committed as a test fixture with its URL and SHA-256. The test **derives** the correspondence rather than assuming it: Bourke's edge→corner pairs are recovered from the XOR structure of his `edgeTable`, then the cube relabelling is found by search. Result: **all 256 cases produce the identical surface, 0 disagreements**, with winding reversed — and `a_single_inside_corner_faces_outward` plus a signed-volume check establish that ours is the outward one. | | |
| | | *Measured, at 49³ unless noted:* sphere 2312 tris (33³) χ=2 · torus 4848 χ=0 genus 1 · box_exact 2696 (33³) χ=2 · csg_difference 4484 (41³) χ=2 · **capped gyroid 24108 tris, χ=−24, genus 13** (the value `expected_euler()` correctly declines to predict) · fbm_terrain 3946 (33³) χ=1, open. Self-intersections **0.000 per 1,000** on a sphere — the baseline A-009 compares the Dual Contouring clamp against. **A grid sample landing exactly on the isosurface produces slivers**: at 25³ over `[-2,2]`, 30 lattice points sit exactly on the unit sphere, giving 96 degenerate triangles and 2.301 intersecting pairs per 1,000 — while χ stays 2. That is sampling, not extraction, and is why degenerates are a recorded metric rather than a gate. | | |
| ☑ | **A-004** | **Surface Nets.** One vertex per sign-changing cell at the centroid of edge crossings, quad or triangle output. Optional Laplacian smoothing passes as a parameter. **Note for the record:** this has no credible published timings anywhere despite being what engines ship — your benchmark will be the reference. | M | T-001 |
| | | **Two claims in the brief and the folklore are measurably false, and this is the ticket that disproved them.** *(a)* The brief expects Surface Nets and Marching Cubes triangle counts "to differ substantially". They differ by **exactly 2χ** — 4 on a sphere, 0 on a torus, 4 on box_exact, 4 on csg_difference, exact on all four. That is forced by Euler: Marching Cubes places one vertex per crossed grid edge, Surface Nets emits two triangles per crossed grid edge, and any closed triangulated surface has `F = 2V − 2χ`, so `F_sn = F_mc + 2χ`. Surface Nets is **not** the cheaper method by triangle count. *(b)* "Every interior vertex has four neighbours" is false once triangulated — measured max degree 10 vs Marching Cubes' 9. What Surface Nets actually buys is quad connectivity and one vertex per *cell* rather than per *edge*. | | |
| | | *And the structural limit, pinned as a measurement.* One vertex per cell means two sheets through one cell are forced to share it, so the output is **non-manifold** exactly where the literature review says it will be: **48 non-manifold edges on the capped gyroid at 49³, 15 on fbm_terrain at 33³** (its highest octave has a wavelength near the cell size, so the terrain folds inside single cells). Orientation and boundary stay clean, so the damage is purely connectivity — "Dual Contouring's actual structural defect", fixed architecturally by A-010's vertex splitting rather than by patching. The test asserts these are non-zero, so the numbers move only when someone means them to. Rounded corners measured too: nearest vertex to `box_exact`'s corner is **1.15 cells** away. | | |

| | | *A trap found while writing it, worth knowing before anyone benchmarks sharp features.* **`box_exact` is exactly zero across its entire boundary** — `f(1,0,0)`, `f(1,1,0)` and `f(1,1,1)` are all `+0` — so a grid plane lying on a box face classifies wholly as *outside* and the sign change moves a cell inward. Consequence: on a grid-aligned box **Marching Cubes lands *further* from the corner than Surface Nets does** (1.41 cells vs 1.15 at 25³), the opposite of the intuition that edge-placed vertices can hit corners. Over the ±2 domain, 25 and 33 samples are grid-aligned and 27 is not (0.71 vs 0.58 cells). **E-104 must use a box that is not grid-aligned**, or it measures the zero-classification rule rather than the algorithm. | |
| ☑ | **A-006** | **Hermite data extraction.** Per sign-changing edge: crossing position (bisection or analytic) **and surface normal there**. `HermiteCell` holding up to 12 crossings. This is Dual Contouring's real input and the reason Dual Contouring can do sharp features at all. **Acceptance:** `hermite_debug` gizmo data is correct on `box_exact` — normals on a flat face are identical, normals across an edge are not. | M | I-003 |
| ☑ | **T-003** | **Accuracy harness.** One-sided and symmetric Hausdorff distance from the mesh to an analytic SDF, sampled on triangle centroids and vertices. Also mean absolute error. **Acceptance:** a unit sphere meshed at 64³ has max error below one cell diagonal. | M | I-003 |
| | | *"64³" means 64 **samples**, so `h = (hi−lo)/63 = 4/63 = 0.063492` and the cell diagonal is `0.10997148`. Recorded because the repo carries a second, conflicting reading: `ThinPlate::CANONICAL_CELL_SIZE = 2·COMPACT_DOMAIN/64` divides by 64 rather than 63. The `mesh()` helper in `marching_cubes/tests.rs` and the SAMPLES-not-cells convention govern, and the difference is 1.6% — enough to matter if someone later commits a golden threshold. | |
| | | *Distance is measured geometrically, not from `\|f(p)\|`, and this is one unconditional path rather than two.* `\|f\|` is a distance only where `\|∇f\| = 1`, which is false for `gyroid` and `fbm_terrain`, so branching on `is_exact_distance()` would put two execution paths in the harness. The obvious branch-free repair `\|f\|/\|∇f\|` is rejected by the field module's own argument — dividing by `\|∇f\|` "introduces a second failure mode wherever `\|∇g\| → 0`" — and is only first order. What ships is the **gradient-flow chord**: Newton-project the sample onto the zero set and measure how far it moved. Exact for the five true distance fields (the first step lands on the surface and its length *is* `\|f\|`), convergent on the other two, and it follows `fields/mod.rs`'s standing instruction that "an accuracy harness should measure against geometry rather than against `\|sample\|`". The bias is an over-estimate, which makes a "below X" gate conservative. | |
| | | *The reverse direction earns its cost, and there is a test that proves it.* Deleting one face of an inscribed octahedron leaves `mesh_to_field` **bit-identical** and moves `field_to_mesh` to `√(3/2 − 2/√3)`. Forward sampling sees misplaced geometry; only reverse sampling sees missing geometry. On real fields it is the reverse number that finds Marching Cubes rounding `box_exact`'s corner (0.1443 against 0.0833 forward) and an under-resolved `thin_plate` (0.0893 against 0.0083). Seeds come from the extractor's own lattice, band-filtered by the first Newton step — deliberately not from sign-changing cells, because a sub-voxel `thin_plate` produces no sign change at all and sign-based seeding would be blind exactly where the mesh is missing. | |
| | | *The stated acceptance criterion is 80× loose and is not what constrains the code.* Marching Cubes measures `1.380e-3` against a `0.10997` threshold, so a harness returning a constant would pass. | | | ***The synthesis produced a result none of the three tickets had on its own: four separate published figures in this project's sources are each one scene's number.*** The greedy-quads `2.76x` measures **1.70x–256x** (M-56); Nielson's `1.3%` manifold-split rate measures **0 on five of seven fields** (M-60); the `54%` contour share measures **13.1%–74.3%** (M-136); and ✗14's "cheapest in the family" is slower on every field on two machines (M-45). Four instances is a pattern rather than a coincidence, and the doc states it as a rule — *ask which field a mesher figure was measured on before believing it, including the ones in this document*. |

| | | ***The answer is 29%, against the 54% the ticket cites, and the biggest stage is not the contour (M-135).*** Mean share across seven fields at two resolutions: **contour 29.0%, weld 25.5%, collider 45.0%, normals 0.4%**. So optimising the extractor alone buys at most **1.41x** on the whole job — which is the ceiling this ticket existed to establish before anyone started. |
| | | ***And the single number is a fiction: the share runs 13.1% to 74.3% (M-136).*** `sphere` 13.1% at the low end, `fbm_terrain` **74.3%** at the high, with a 5.7x spread on identical code. The variable is how expensive the *field* is to sample — fBm noise swamps the fixed post-processing, a cheap analytic field does not. So "is it worth optimising the contour" has to be answered per workload, and the share rises with resolution everywhere because the contour is `O(n³)` while the post-passes scale with triangle count. |

And the collider check runs on the **welded** mesh, because M-96 records that a validity measurement on unwelded output is meaningless and G-005's contract is welded to begin with. |

| | | ***Round trip verified over a hash of the whole world, and it cannot pass vacuously.*** FNV-1a over every position and index, so one vertex moving by one bit anywhere fails it. It answers on ops alone and cannot see shapes, which is exactly where its conservatism lives: disjoint brushes commute whatever their ops, so the same audit on a disjoint fixture returns those 2 pairs as conservative. | | | ***The field is the whole ticket.*** `solid(p) = max(p.y - height(x,z), |gyroid(p)| - t)` — a `max` is an intersection, so rock exists only where a point is below the surface *and* inside a thickened gyroid. The gyroid is triply periodic, so it tunnels in x, y **and** z, and the result has arches, connected caves and ceilings. Nine lines, nothing authored, and none of it has a height. |
| | | ***The gyroid's period is the entire look, and the first attempt got it wrong by 2.6x.*** At `K = 0.19` the period is 33 m — one tunnel is wider than the view and the world reads as a cracked plain. At `K = 0.5` it is 12.6 m and several arches are in frame at once. |

This is M-72 arriving by composition rather than by resolution. |

| | | ***The headline number is a cost, and it is bad: 241–272 ms per fragment, worst 369 ms.*** A 60 fps frame is 16.7 ms, so one fragment's decomposition is **14–22 whole frames**, charged on the frame the shot lands. Its doc comment had asserted the opposite (*"ties need no tie-break"*) since ✗12, and survived 9600 measured trials because `dot_equivariant`'s terms are products of two components, where a signed permutation flips both signs and the terms permute without negating. The tie-break now compares the signed values. |
| | | ***And the property the ticket named is not fully reachable — the bound is now on record rather than assumed (M-177).*** `φ(−S) = −φ(S)` cannot be had from any ordering rule: a magnitude tie group holds `m` copies of `−c` and `n` of `+c`, negation swaps the counts, and no multiset-derived order maps a group onto its own reverse unless `m == n`. Since a lattice rotation can negate a component, a sum of *components* is not bit-exactly equivariant under the full octahedral group by this route; the three-term dot product is, for M-175's reason. **What is delivered is the weaker and sufficient property**: the vertex is a function of the crossings and not of the edge labels they arrived under, tested by `the_vertex_does_not_depend_on_which_edges_the_crossings_arrived_on` with a negative control beside it. Anything stronger needs exact summation, not a better sort. |

It settled three things the prose does not. The paper's own listing of the inner hexagon is **corrupt** in the copy held here, assigning `p₁` and `p₂` the same triple; *"three quadratic equations"* is really one, the other two coordinates following by linear evaluation; and the tunnel-versus-twelve-vertex split is decided by the **contour count**, not by the asymptote-side predicate of Proposition 1 that the prose never pins down. **So the rule-5 stop A-002h was pre-emptively flagged for never had to be taken.** |

(4) *and* with the authors' program, which groups them differently. Checked against a direct evaluation at nine values of `u` over 20,000 cells: worst disagreement **1.33e-15**. Also pinned: **Grosso's corner numbering is this crate's**, which is a coincidence rather than a design and now fails loudly if `cube.rs` ever renumbers. |
| | | ***The headline measurement is an agreement nobody predicted (M-206).*** `interior::SweptFaces` solves a quadratic in the sweep **height**; this solves one in the face **coordinate** and interpolates. They coincide anyway, to **1.13e-12** over 1,076 cells. Without a closure the cell emits a patch with a boundary no neighbour shares. `the_tunnel_patch_is_manifold_inside_the_cell` caught it on its first run. |
| | | ***And the closure's winding cannot be fixed, which took two wrong attempts to establish.*** A twelve-vertex ring circles the hexagon in either direction depending on the configuration, so the fan's orientation is derived from the hexagon edges the ring walk actually laid. Both fixed windings were rejected by the directed-edge check — which is why that check is directed and not merely a count. |
| | | ***The acceptance: 2,297 patches, every one manifold and consistently wound inside the cell.*** Each non-contour edge traversed exactly once in each direction, each contour edge exactly once because its second face belongs to the neighbouring cell. **That is the property Chernyaev's tunnel triangulation fails** — his lays part of the tunnel *on* the ambiguous face, so two neighbours both claim it — and it is the entire reason this route needs no grid-subdivision pass. Also measured: the three-hexagon-step case, which the construction has no rule for, fires **zero** times, and is returned as a count rather than asserted so a caller cannot mistake a hole for a closed patch. |

| ☑ | **E-217** | **`game_dig` gets out of the way, stays fast under a held button, falls under gravity, and offers the GPU as a peer.** | L | E-202, G-006, GPU-005 |
| | | ***The FPS collapse was arithmetic, not mystery, and three mechanisms were needed rather than one.*** A four-second hold pushed ~200 brushes because the distance gate admits one edit per *frame*, and `game_dig` was the only game example calling `mesh_dirty` — draining the whole queue synchronously — rather than `DirtySet::mesh_within_budget`. So: the dirty set now survives the frame and drains nearest-first under a 4 ms budget (`fn rebuild` deleted outright, `drain_dirty` is the only place a chunk is meshed), a held button edits at a fixed **20 a second**, and each chunk meshes against a Lipschitz-pruned tape. **Measured: the 256-chunk startup fill drains in 16 frames**, and a switch that used to block for most of a second is now a modal you watch fill in. |
| | | ***The pruner is transcribed from `tape_pruning.rs` and its licence is bit-exactness, which is now a test rather than a claim.*** `prune_into` runs at both sites — per chunk in `drain_dirty` and over the edit box in `dig` — and the gate asserts the mesh is **bit-identical on all seven CPU extractors across eight chunks** and that `EditReport` and the dirty set are unchanged, because E1 is the number this example exists to publish. Paired with a **count** clause that the pruner actually fired (best chunk keeps ≤ half the tape), since a pruner that returns the whole tape passes an equality test and buys nothing — and a timing measurement cannot tell the two apart. |
| | | ***The gaps on keys 4, 5 and 6 were one line of loop arithmetic and are closed by one borrowed cell layer.*** `dual.rs`'s walk skips the outermost quad plane on every face, so a chunk given only its own cells stops one cell short and neither neighbour bridges it — structural, and true only of a chunk given nothing else. `Algorithm::halo_cells()` is 1 for the three dual methods and 0 for the edge-based families, which already tile; `dig` then expands the dirty set over the **negative octant** rather than three faces, because a cell on a chunk corner is borrowed by all seven chunks below it and face-only expansion leaves a notch at exactly the corner the halo exists to fix. The gate is geometric and exact: a halo'd mesh must put a vertex **past** the shared plane and an edge-based one must not. |
| | | ***Walking found a real defect the first version shipped: a frictionless body slid downhill for ever.*** Collision samples the field under two spheres — no collider, because M-116 puts a convex decomposition at 241–272 ms per fragment and M-135 puts the collider check at 45% of a usable mesh, and this demo edits the field on every frame of a held button. Integrating gravity while grounded made a resting body sink 5 mm a frame, which depenetration then pushed back out along the surface *normal*; on a slope that has a horizontal component, so it accumulated **−1.76 u/s** of downhill velocity. `gravity_step` gives a standing body nothing to slide with. **No friction and no slope limit remain, deliberately**: dig a pit with vertical walls and you can still walk out of it. M-172's zero gradient on the medial axis is handled by pushing `+Y`, which is the only direction that means anything inside rock. |
| | | ***The eighth mesher required making `isomesh-gpu` reach the browser, and there was exactly one hard blocker.*** `webgpu` joins the unconditional wgpu backend list (omitting it links **zero** backends on wasm32 with no compile error), 7 `std::time::Instant` sites become `web_time::Instant`, and `read_bytes_many_deferred` is `read_bytes_many` with the wait taken out — `Device::poll` is a documented no-op under WebGPU and `map_async` completes only from the event loop, so the mpsc wait deadlocks the tab. `extract_indirect` is the only extraction entry point that reads nothing back, which is why it is the one used. **Verified on the RTX 3090: key `8` leaves 64 chunks resident, exactly the count key `1` produced**, zero refused readbacks, and the HUD prints where the time went with the upload dominating. |
| | | ***Turning on `bevy`'s `webgpu` feature moves all nine web demos, not one.*** Cargo features are per-package and `bevy_render` gives `webgpu` precedence over `webgl2` on wasm32, so there is no per-example choice; `web/play.html` gates every demo on `navigator.gpu` and `web/lite.js`'s "the nine playable demos need it too" became false and was rewritten. The front page's own 130 KB module is still WebGL2, because it is hand-written GL rather than a Bevy build. |
| | | ***The visual half of the acceptance could not be run on this host, and that is recorded rather than glossed.*** Headless Chrome cannot create a WebGPU swap-chain shared image here — `Could not find SharedImageBackingFactory with params: …WebgpuSwapChainTexture…`, reproduced by a twelve-line bare WebGPU clear containing none of this code, on four flag sets — and there is no reachable display for a native run. So the screenshots became tests: 13 in `cargo test --example game_dig`, including the modal being up **exactly** while a backlog drains, **exactly ten edits in forty 16 ms frames** where the old code made forty, and the jump and mode keys reaching the body through the real systems. What was verified in the browser is that all nine modules instantiate under WebGPU with no shader, pipeline or adapter error, and that the `navigator.gpu` guard shows its message. **Note for whoever has a display: the pixels are unverified.** |
| ☑ | **T-011** | **Committed metric baselines and a regression diff.** | M | — |
| | | ***It earned its keep on the first run (M-242).*** X-001 had just rewritten how `benches/shootout.rs` enumerates its algorithms, which touches every measurement the file produces. Re-run and compared row for row: **112 rows, zero differences** in vertices, triangles or non-manifold edges. That is precisely the change golden hashes cannot see — T-007 pins meshes from the extractors, not from the bench — and *"the diff looked mechanical"* is not evidence. |
| | | ***Two classes of metric, and only one is noisy.*** Vertices, triangles and non-manifold edges are compared **exactly**: they are deterministic by T-004 and a tolerance there could only hide a real change. `hausdorff` gets 2% and `self_intersections_per_1k` 5%, for float accumulation across architectures. `median_ms` gets **60%** — a tripwire for a doubling, not a benchmark, because wall clock moves with the governor and whatever else is running. |
| | | ***Baselines are per machine and the machine is in the filename***, matching the `resolution_sweep-ryzen9-5900x.csv` convention already used by hand. A run on another host finds no baseline and says so, rather than comparing against numbers that never applied to it. A timing baseline from another box is worse than none. |
| | | ***The acceptance is that the gate has been seen to fail, three ways.*** `--self-test` doubles one row's `median_ms` in a copy and requires the failure to **name the row** — it reports *"sphere qef 17: median_ms 0.396 → 0.793 (+100.0%, tolerance 60%)"*. Two real perturbations were also run and caught: a Hausdorff worsened 50% against its 2% band, and a triangle count moved by **two**, which the exact comparison catches where any tolerance would not. It runs in CI, because the half that rots silently is the checker rather than the numbers. |
| | | *Deviation from the ticket, with the reason: it is `scripts/regress.sh` rather than `cargo run --bin regress`. A `[[bin]]` in `crates/isomesh` would ship an executable to every consumer of a `no_std` library and appear in `cargo install`, and the repo already has four gates as scripts — `backlog_gate.sh`, `readme_sync.sh`, `findings_index.sh`, `record_gif.sh` — so this is the existing idiom rather than a new one.* |

The gate still passed: command substitution failing does not fail the script. | ☑ | **F-001** | **Replace `is_exact_distance() -> bool` with a declared bound.** | M | — |
| | | ***Both sources verified in the corpus rather than cited from the ticket.*** Bálint, Valasek & Gergó 2019 (`10.14232/actacyb.24.1.2019.3`) Corollary 1, verbatim: *"Every signed distance function is Lipschitz continuous and their smallest Lipschitz constant is 1."* Their 2023 follow-up (`10.14733/cadaps.2023.1154-1174`) supplies `q` and is blunt about why exactness cannot survive CSG: *"the minimum of two exact signed distance functions… is not an exact SDF, and the error can be arbitrarily large under certain conditions."* |
| | | ***`FieldBound` has four cases because a `bool` could hold neither half of `true // away from the seam`.*** `Exact`, `Lipschitz { l }`, `Underestimate { q }`, `Unbounded`. The split that matters: `l` bounds how fast the field *changes* and survives arbitrary CSG, which is what Phase 12 needs; `q` bounds how far the *value* is from the distance and does not. |
| | | ***The test caught its own author, immediately (M-244).*** The first draft declared `noise_cavity` as `Lipschitz { l: 2.598 }`; `every_field_meets_the_bound_it_declares` measured `|∇f|` reaching **7.734** and failed. That is the same defect the ticket existed to remove, reproduced one screen away by the person removing it. **The gyroid's constant was guessed too and survived only by luck** — `√3` declared against a sampled maximum of 1.695. Derived properly: `|∂g/∂x| ≤ 2`, so `|∇g| ≤ 2√3 ≈ 3.464`, twice the guess and in the direction where being wrong lets a tracer step through the surface. |
| | | ***`noise_cavity` is `Unbounded`, not measured.*** A sampled maximum is a lower bound on a supremum, so declaring one as a Lipschitz constant would be unsound in the dangerous direction. F-002 is where a real constant gets established from the noise's amplitude and octaves. |
| | | *Acceptance met: every field declares, `csg_difference` is no longer `Exact` and has its own pinned test, and `accuracy.rs`, `shootout` and `ablation` all gate on `bound().is_exact()`. One rotting claim fell out — `accuracy.rs` said Hausdorff is unavailable for "two of the seven" fields; it is **four of the eight**, and nothing could check that until each field declared.* |
| ☑ | **F-002** | **A Lipschitz-bound validator, in the harness.** | M | F-001 |
| | | ***The validator is one-sided, and the asymmetry is the design.*** A sampled maximum is a **lower** bound on a supremum, so this can prove a declaration wrong and can never prove one right. Finding `‖∇f‖ = 7.73` against a declared 2.598 settles it; finding nothing above 1.7 against a declared 3.46 says only that the sampling missed. `violates()` therefore asks a one-sided question, and `a_loosened_declaration_is_never_a_violation` pins that as a property rather than leaving it to be read off the code. |
| | | ***It found something that justifies F-001's shape (M-245).*** `csg_difference` measures **100% eikonal** while not being a distance: away from the seam the active operand *is* an exact distance, and the seam is measure-zero. **So `|∇f| ≈ 1` is necessary and not sufficient**, and the obvious single-number validator — check the field is eikonal — would have passed the exact field this phase exists because of. That is why `FieldBound` carries `l` and `q` separately, and it is now asserted rather than argued. |
| | | ***The acceptance is that a tightened declaration fails.*** `tightening_a_declaration_by_one_step_is_caught` replaces each field's real bound with the next tighter one and requires the report to catch it — three fields tightened and caught, five already at their tightest, both counts asserted so the test cannot quietly stop testing anything. |
| | | *The census is recorded because it is interesting in its own right: sup `‖∇f‖` and eikonal fraction are 1.000/100% for the four exact fields and for `csg_difference`, 1.727/67.0% for gyroid, 2.850/11.7% for fbm_terrain, and 7.748/85.6% for noise_cavity — whose pairing of a high eikonal fraction with a gradient reaching 7.7 is a second way the fraction alone misleads.* |
| ☑ | **F-003** | **CSG combinators that propagate the bound.** | M | F-002 |
| | | ***The ticket's prediction is refuted, with numbers (M-246).*** It expected `min` of two exact fields to yield a bound F-002 confirms and `max` to yield *"a strictly weaker one"*. Measured against closed-form ground truth over 64,000 points: **union is exact outside (0.000e0) and wrong inside by 6.989e-1; intersection is exact inside (0.000e0) and wrong outside by 6.995e-1** — a ratio of 0.999. They are mirror images. There *is* an asymmetry and it is by **region**, not by operator. |
| | | ***What composes is the Lipschitz constant; what does not is exactness, and no `q` is invented.*** `min`/`max` of an `l₁`- and an `l₂`-Lipschitz function is `max(l₁,l₂)`-Lipschitz, exactly, which is what keeps a sphere tracer's step size valid through an arbitrary CSG tree. Precision does not: Bálint, Valasek & Gergó's Theorem 6 gives the survivor as `¼·σ(δ)/diam·min(q_f,q_g)`, where `σ` is a **set-contact smoothness** depending on how the solids meet. This crate does not compute `σ`, so a composed field reports `Lipschitz` and stops — a number derived from a factor nobody evaluated is a guess with a citation attached. |
| | | ***`BoundedSdf` is separate from `ReferenceField` on purpose.*** That trait is about test fixtures and also demands a domain, a closedness flag and an expected Euler characteristic, none of which a CSG node has any business answering. The new trait asks one question, so a combinator can answer it from its operands — and `composed_bound` is one definition shared by all four, because the rule is identical and four copies would drift. |
| | | *An `Unbounded` operand poisons the composition, asserted: nothing can be claimed about a value composed from a value nothing is claimed about.* |
| ☑ | **F-004** | **Measure how fast the distance property degrades under repeated CSG.** | M | F-003 |
| | | ***The ticket's proposed metric could not have seen the thing it was measuring.*** F-004 said to sample `‖∇f‖`. F-002 had since measured `csg_difference` at **100% eikonal** while its values are not distances (M-245), because `max` selects an exact operand pointwise and the seam is measure-zero. The bench keeps `‖∇f‖` as a **control column**, and it reads 100.0% at every stroke count from 0 to 256 — a flat line, exactly as predicted. |
| | | ***What degrades is the tail, and only the tail (M-247).*** Empirical underestimate ratio over 13,824 points: worst case **0.5774 → 0.1815 → 0.0726 → 0.0040** at 0, 4, 32 and 256 strokes, **143× down**, while the **median stays at 1.0000 throughout**. |
| | | ***So the ticket's question has two answers, and the useful one is not the one it asked for.*** *"No longer a distance"* happens within a handful of strokes; *"no longer usable"* has not happened at 256, where mean sphere-tracing cost has gone **5.2 → 9.9 steps**. A destructible game should watch the tracing cost rather than the precision bound. |
| | | *The caveat is in the measurement rather than the field, and is stated in the output rather than buried: `q̂` is built from a **ray** distance, and a ray leaving a box corner runs along the diagonal, so an **uncarved** box reports `q̂_min = 0.5774 ≈ 1/√3`. That is the metric's floor. The curve is read against that baseline, not against 1.0, and reporting the absolute number would have called an exact box degraded.* |
| ☑ | **F-005** | **Empty-cell rejection by sphere tracing — the attack on M-98's 70×.** | M | F-001 |
| | | ***One evaluation replaces 576, and the spread is geometric (M-248).*** Cost against Marching Cubes **before → after**: sphere 204× → 36.7×, torus 294× → 45.6×, box_exact 381× → 88.9×, csg_difference 400× → 91.4×, thin_plate 389× → **32.9×**, gyroid 449× → 295×. `thin_plate` gains **11.8×** because a plate leaves nearly all its domain empty; `gyroid` gains **1.5×** because a triply periodic surface reaches almost every cell. |
| | | ***A loose constant is taxed twice, which is a second reason F-001's had to be derived.*** The rejection radius is `l·(√3/2)·h`, so gyroid's `l = 3.46` inflates it by that factor and disqualifies cells a distance field would have rejected — the optimisation pays in proportion to emptiness and is charged for imprecision. |
| | | ***Bit-identical output is the safety property, and it is checked rather than argued.*** A rejection test that is ever wrong produces a **hole**, and a hole is invisible to every validity gate in this repository: the mesh is simply missing a piece and stays perfectly manifold, closed and correctly oriented. `rejection_does_not_change_the_mesh` compares both paths byte for byte on every field with a constant. |
| | | *`None` is the default and the only safe answer when the constant is unknown, which is why `without_a_constant_no_cell_is_rejected` pins that too. A constant smaller than the field's true one rejects cells containing surface — and M-244 is the incident where a hand-reasoned constant was wrong by 3× on the first attempt.* |
| ☑ | **F-006** | **Segment tracing / enhanced sphere tracing.** | M | F-005 |
| | | ***A null result on five fields of six, which is what the ticket asked to be told (M-249).*** Galin et al. state the condition for their own method's failure: *"when the implicit objects have an almost uniform distribution of primitives and a uniform Lipschitz bound over their support Ω, the benefit is limited or negative."* `sphere`, `torus`, `box_exact`, `csg_difference` and `thin_plate` are 1-Lipschitz **everywhere**, so no directional bound can be smaller than 1. Steps global → directional: 228 → 228, 360 → 360, 108 → 108, 108 → 108, 148 → 148 — **asserted as equality**, not as a small difference. |
| | | ***The one field that can gain, gains 1.80×, and its bound is derived rather than sampled.*** Along a coordinate axis the gyroid's directional derivative is a single partial, `|∂g/∂x| = |cos a cos b − sin c sin a| ≤ 2`, against the global `|∇g| ≤ 2√3`. Steps **2184 → 1213** — slightly better than the 1.73× the bound ratio predicts, because fewer steps also accumulate less conservatism. |
| | | *So the technique is worth exactly what a field's global bound is loose by. That is the sentence to carry forward: it is not a general acceleration, it is a correction for imprecise bounds, and an analytic distance primitive has none to correct.* |

> **SCOPED 2026-08-17 on M-319, and the measurement VALIDATES this ticket rather than closing it.** The cheap escape was worth checking first: if filling rarely disconnected anything, this would collapse from *implement dynamic connectivity* to *detect the rare split and recompute*. It does not. **About one fill in six changes the air component count** — 16% at 65³ on `noise_cavity`, from 200 brush fills with the count rebuilt rather than maintained. A detect-and-recompute design would rebuild once every six edits at `O(n³)`, which is exactly the cost R-022 exists to avoid. **Read the 65³ row**: the fills accumulate, and 33³ ends with only 29.3% of its air left, so its 41% is largely the domain being eaten, where 65³ ends at 84.5%.
> 
> **RESIZED 2026-08-17 on M-320, and the ticket got substantially smaller.** The same 200 fills, seen two ways. **Clause 1 held:** ~**two thirds of deleted edges are non-tree** and therefore free — 61.2% → 63.8% → **64.8%** against a closed form of `1 - n/(3(n-1))` ≈ 66%, below it and rising toward it as the air region's surface-to-volume ratio falls. A constant factor of 3, not an asymptotic win.
> 
> **Clause 2 was left unpredicted and it is the one that resizes this.** D-Tree's replacement search costs the size of the **smaller** side of the split. **That size is 1 at the median, at every resolution**; the largest seen anywhere is 120 against 227,567 air samples, 0.05% of the domain. A sphere advancing into a cave strands single fringe voxels rather than severing passages mid-span.
> 
> **So do not build HDT.** The `O(log n)` levels, the demotion of non-replacement edges, the whole amortisation argument, exist to bound a search whose cost can otherwise be a constant fraction of the graph — and here it is one voxel. What remains is the older technique HDT also uses: **alternating BFS outward from the two endpoints of the deleted tree edge, stopping when either side exhausts**, which is `O(smaller side)` without needing to know in advance which side is smaller. No levels, no demotion, no amortisation scheme, and **no new dependency** — rule 3 is satisfied by construction.
> 
> **Register the `P-` against `O(k log² n)` amortized** (Acar et al.'s batch-dynamic HDT, `10.48550/arXiv.2205.04956`) — *not* against `O(k log(1+n/k))`, which is the batch-ETT **tree** bound and appears only as a factor inside the per-level ETT cost. Registering against the tree bound would let a structure pass while doing unbounded replacement-search work, which is where every constant factor lives. Given M-320 the realistic target is far below that ceiling; state both.
> 
> **Two structures in the change, and the second is the easy one.** Splits outnumber emptyings **27:5** — a fill can *sever* a component or *consume* a small pocket entirely, and a consumed component needs no replacement edge. **And the rate is a brush-to-feature ratio, not a constant**: radius 4 in 65³ is about 6% of the domain per axis, which is a large brush, and `noise_cavity` is deliberately near its own feature size — the adversarial end. What is established is *tens of percent*, not the fraction of a percent that would have justified recomputing.
> 
> **So this is a real build, and rule 3 forbids a dependency**: batch-dynamic connectivity from scratch, with the replacement-edge search that `10.48550/arXiv.1908.01956`'s sketching exists for. Register the `P-` against a bound rather than a stopwatch, the way M-311 did: `O(k log(1 + n/k))` work, and the deterministic bounds a bounded-degree lattice buys (V-41).
> **SPLIT 2026-08-16 before measuring, on V-41 — the hypothesis is two problems and the ticket named neither.** Durfee et al. state the asymmetry plainly: *"An **insert** can cause at most two trees in `F` to be joined"*, while *"a **delete** may split a tree into two"* and then needs a **replacement-edge search**, which is what the sketching apparatus in that paper exists for. Mapped onto play: **digging** makes air nodes appear — insertion only, and a union-find answers it; **filling** makes them vanish — deletion, and that is where the polylogarithmic machinery and its constants live. Measuring digging and reporting it as *dynamic connectivity* would be the easy half wearing the hard half's name, so **R-022a** takes the insertion-only case and **R-022b** the fully dynamic one.
> 
> **Two things V-41 banks that make this cheaper than the ticket assumed.** `validate::sealing` already builds the air-sublevel union-find on a sample lattice, so R-022a is a harness around existing code rather than a new structure. And a 6-connected voxel graph is **bounded degree**, which is precisely the restriction that forces ad-hoc work on the social and web graphs these structures were benchmarked on (`10.48550/arXiv.2506.16477`) — so the lattice is the *easy* case for RC-trees, not a stress test, and the bounds are deterministic rather than randomized. **Read against the paper's own bound rather than a stopwatch:** `O(k log(1 + n/k))`, which at `n = 128³` and a brush-sized `k ≈ 10³` is a factor of about **11**, so ~10⁴ work units — that is what makes 1 ms plausible and is the number a harness should be compared with.
> **DONE 2026-08-17 — M-321 / P-26, and the shape of the answer is not the shape the ticket predicted.** This row expected the polylogarithmic machinery: RC-trees, bounded degree as the lever, deterministic rather than randomised bounds. **None of that was built, because measurement said it was not the binding constraint.** M-319: one fill in six disconnects, so the cheap escape does not exist. M-320: the smaller side of a split is **1 voxel at the median**, so the levelled HDT scheme is amortising a case this lattice does not present. ✗26: a union-find cannot absorb deletion at all — parent pointers encode union history, not adjacency, so re-rooting a shed piece severs its **descendants** — and the structure went **flat**, which made `connected` `O(1)` and `&self`.
> 
> **What shipped:** `Air::fill`, `Air::repair`, `Air::label_of`, `Air::pending`, budgeted via the same `spend: FnMut() -> bool` shape as `mesh_within_budget`, with both directions of staleness conservative — an unfinished fill reads *"not sealed yet"* and an unfinished dig reads *"not connected yet"*. M-321: **3.09 → 3.38 visited per seed** while the lattice grows 7.6×, and **436×** better than rebuilding at 65³.
> 
> **The tail is real and is measured rather than waved at**: a deliberate tunnel bisection costs **1.1× a full rebuild**, because lockstep stops only after walking half the component and there is no replacement edge to find. **R-028** carries the remedy, which is decomposition rather than a better search.

After this they deliberately differ — seven keys walk the survivors per sample on the CPU, the eighth uploads the log and folds it on the device — and that difference *is* the finding key `8` now demonstrates. The HUD prints `base … (cached)` and `fold` separately, plus the honest verdict: at 17³ the CPU wins (0.06 ms against 0.22, M-296), because a fixed setup cost cannot amortise over 4,913 samples. **A 17³ chunk is the one row in that table where the GPU loses**, and a demo that offered a GPU key while saying nothing invited the opposite assumption.
>
> ***Nothing here ports a second extractor to the GPU, and the reason is measured.*** `count + emit` is **0.045 ms at 129³** and flat across a 420× rise in cell count (M-296), so a second GPU extractor would optimise a term that is already neither large nor growing. `docs/research/2026-08-11-meshing-speed-analysis.md:110-113` ranks per-cell arithmetic fourth at 1.5–3.9×, which is *the entire spread between extraction algorithms* — rank 4 of 4. Media Molecule's production note that Dual Contouring is the easy one on a GPU (fixed one-vertex-per-cell output) and this repo's own `emit_quads` wall at **IPC 0.72 against 3.83** both say the dual methods would port well; they would port well into a term that is not the cost.
>
> ***Verification.*** `fold_into` against `BrushStack` over an uploaded non-`GpuField` base: worst deviation **4.77e-7** over 25³ samples with an add, a subtract and a smooth add in the log, inside M-157's 8.4e-7 for edit-log agreement; an empty fold is the base **bit for bit**; a base of a different sample count returns `SampleCountMismatch`. `isomesh-gpu` 13/13 `field_sampler` tests, `game_dig` 14/14 — including `the_gpu_mesher_agrees_with_the_cpu_one` **unchanged**, which after this change is the stronger claim of the two: the CPU walks `BrushStack` per sample while the GPU folds the same log in a compute shader, so the triangle counts agreeing means the two field paths agree.

Cause 2 was `contact = Some(n)` **inside** the resolve loop, so velocity cancelled against whichever sphere came last in `BODY_OFFSETS` rather than the deepest overlap — a body with its head in a lip and its feet on the floor cancelled against the head. Cause 3 is arity: two spheres to four needs `RESOLVE_PASSES` 2 → 3, twelve sample-and-gradient pairs a frame against eight.

| ☑ | **D-014** | M | D-013 |
> **DONE 2026-08-26 — the floor and the walls stop the player, the frame rate and the mesher survive a hidden panel, and the GPU job cap bounds something for the first time.** Two user-reported defects, and a third found while gating the first.
>
> **1. Digging out the bottom dropped the player through the floor (✗48 / M-369).** D-013's own reasoning was *"no `y` clamp — the field already stops descent, and the floor wall is scenery"*, and it was wrong about where the field stops. `aim` refuses a brush *centred* outside `sandbox`, but a brush centred **on** the floor plane reaches its own radius below it — up to `2.00` against a floor at `y = -5.4` — so a shaft dug to the bottom removes the field under the box while the chunks and their meshes stop at `-5.4`. The body left the visible world and fell until it met whatever `Ground` still had, embedded in rock nobody can see or dig.
>
> ***A `y` clamp could not have fixed it, and that is the more useful half.*** Clamping a coordinate stops the fall without ever reporting ground, so the body hangs at the limit with `grounded` false, the jump refused, and `gravity_step` accelerating into a surface it is not allowed to touch. The boundary has to be in the **field** the resolver samples, so depenetration, the ground probe and the jump all see it — which is also what deleted D-013's `x`/`z` clamp, a second path doing the same job worse. `Walls` is five half-spaces built from the same `sandbox()` call `walls()` draws from, unioned with the brush stack **for collision only**: the mesher must not see them, because they are already on screen as five cuboids and meshing them would draw them twice. Half-spaces rather than the 0.5-thick slabs deliberately — the body only ever touches an inner face, and a half-space has no far side for one fast frame to tunnel through.
>
> ***No collision meshes, and that is the same answer D-013 gave.*** The ask was for collision *meshes*; what shipped is collision, without them. This demo's entire premise is that it has no collider cache because it edits the field on every frame of a held button (M-116: 241–272 ms per fragment for a convex decomposition), so adding a mesh collider for the walls would be a second collision system in the one demo built to prove none is needed. The outcome asked for — you cannot sink through the floor — is delivered by the field.
>
> **2. The frame rate went with the panel.** `update_hud`'s `!flags.hud` branch printed only the hint, so `game_dig` — which *opens* with the panel hidden — showed the mesher on its banner and nothing about cost. The frame rate now joins the hint line, which is the `[H] HUD` line the ask named; it goes on the hint rather than the banner because the banner already carries the mesher, so neither is duplicated when the panel is open. `nohud` still yields an **empty** frame, which the nine committed GIFs depend on, and that is asserted rather than assumed.
>
> **3. `GPU_JOBS_MAX` bounded nothing (✗47 / M-367), found by the load the D-013 tests added.** The cap was the second clause of `mesh_within_budget`'s budget predicate — and that predicate is consulted **after** meshing a chunk, deliberately, so a budget too small for one chunk still makes progress. So a frame beginning at the cap dispatched one more regardless, and since that repeats on every frame in which no readback retires, the queue grew by one per frame with **no bound**: 17 at frame 39, then **18** once the assertion was loosened to `cap + 1`. Two fixes that look right were tried and measured wrong first: *refusing to enter the drain while full* stalls the switch outright (a frame that dispatches nothing defers every chunk, and the overshoot was what had been carrying the drain), and *asserting `cap + 1`* is the first term of a series rather than a bound. What holds is checking `in_flight` **before** `gpu_dispatch` and putting the refused chunk back in the dirty set — deferred, not dropped, and not quietly meshed on the CPU either, because key `8` means the device meshed it.
>
> ***And the cap was being compared against a stale number (M-368).*** `drain_dirty` seeded its in-flight count from `pending.jobs.len()` while running **before** `gpu_collect` in the same chained frame, so it counted every job the device had already finished and nothing had retired. With the cap enforced and the order left alone, a 256-chunk switch collapsed to **one chunk per twelve frames** with the queue pinned at 16 for 900 frames. `gpu_collect` now runs first: retire, then dispatch into the freed slots. A job dispatched this frame is still collected next frame at the earliest, so the latency is unchanged and the suite went back under a second.
>
> ***The 900-frame guard was an assumption about the machine, and it is gone.*** It was chosen when this drain took 135 frames on an idle device, and a red *"the GPU switch never drained"* about a correctly-working demo is what a fixed count buys. Every drain-wait in the test module now goes through one `drain` helper that asserts the job cap on every frame and gates **progress** rather than speed: the outstanding count must decrease within 1200 frames, which is machine-independent because a live device always retires something. Six fixed loops became one helper.
>
> ***Verification.*** `cargo test --example game_dig` **26/26 over eight consecutive default-parallelism runs**. Both fixes mutation-tested: removing `Walls` from `move_camera`'s union walks the body to `x = 42.1` and fails `walking_into_the_wall_stops_at_the_sandbox`, which gates the *wiring* while `the_collision_boundary_is_solid_exactly_where_the_slabs_are` gates the *field* on all five faces and `digging_through_the_floor_lands_the_body_on_it_rather_than_losing_it` reproduces the reported bug and its fixture's premise. `a_hidden_panel_still_shows_the_frame_rate_and_the_mesher` drives `update_hud` itself — the `!flags.hud` early return is the branch that dropped the number, and a test that formatted its own line would not cross it — and checks the `nohud` empty frame in the same test, because the two requirements pull opposite ways. `preflight --full` **23 ok, all green**. The rendered image is still unverified on this host for D-013's reasons: no display, no Xvfb, no passwordless sudo.

> **DONE 2026-08-26 — the retired hostname now says `NXDOMAIN` instead of impersonating an outage.** D-013 cleared `isomesh.ladvien.com` from the repository's Pages settings and stopped there, which left its Route 53 `CNAME` still pointing at `ladvien.github.io` — the worst of the three states that name can be in. It **resolved**, so `https://isomesh.ladvien.com/index.html` failed the TLS handshake (`curl` exit 60: no certificate for that host, which is the certificate that never provisioned in the first place) and `http://` returned GitHub's own 404 for a `Host` it no longer maps. Both read as *the site is down*, and that is how it was reported.
>
> **Deleted in the Route 53 console rather than by CLI, deliberately.** One-off deletion of one record, in the zone that also holds the apex serving the personal site: the console shows the row before it commits, which is the property worth having when the blast radius includes `ladvien.com`. The CLI path needed a fresh key anyway — the credentials on `big` have been invalid since 24 April — and the snippet first offered for it was bash on a **fish** login shell, where `ZONE=$(…)` is not an assignment at all (`fish: Unsupported use of '='`). `CLAUDE.md` names the shell; the snippet ignored it.
>
> ***Scope, measured before deciding.*** The pretty URL was worth keeping only if anything immutable pointed at it, and nothing did: published in `README.md` for **two days** (`8b830a0` 2026-08-24 → `435fea7` 2026-08-26), **no** git tags in the repository, **zero** commits touching the domain in any of the three crate READMEs, and 0.0.9 shipped 2026-08-17 — a week before the site existed — with no version bump since, so crates.io and docs.rs never carried it. Zero clickable old-domain links on the deployed pages. The only holder was one bookmark.
>
> ***The redirect was considered and rejected on cost.*** An S3 redirect bucket or CloudFront distribution with an ACM cert would make the old URL work over HTTPS, and it is four resources plus a certificate maintained permanently to serve a two-day-old bookmark. The tempting variant — CloudFront in front of `ladvien.github.io/isomesh/` so the pretty domain serves the site *directly* with a valid ACM cert, bypassing GitHub's custom-domain machinery entirely — is rejected for a sharper reason: it puts a second cache in front of the artefact, and *"fresh page prose over a stale wasm module"* is the exact failure this skill exists to catch. Every deploy would grow an invalidation step and every verification would have to see through two CDNs. Recorded here so it is not re-litigated as an obvious win.
>
> ***Verification.*** No answer from `1.1.1.1`, `8.8.8.8` or `9.9.9.9`; the authoritative nameserver returns the zone SOA for the name. The apex is untouched — `ladvien.com` still resolves to its four CloudFront addresses and still serves `200` — which was the one real risk in editing that zone. `https://ladvien.github.io/isomesh/`, `/index.html` and `/play.html` all `200` with `redirects=0`. The skill gained the `dig` pair as a standing check, including the apex line, because "did I delete only the one row" is worth one command.

| ☑ | **D-016** | S | — |
> **DONE 2026-08-26 — a stranger's TCP reset no longer reddens a docs-only push.** `publish.sh`'s crates.io version probe was an un-retried `curl`, and at D-015 it failed a whole CI run on `curl (35) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer` — on the **third** crate, two crates after two clean probes in the same second, for a commit that touched four markdown files. The site had already deployed successfully in the same run; only `package (dry run)` was red, and `publish to crates.io` was skipped behind it.
>
> ***The interesting part is that the script's careful arm was unreachable.*** Its `case` has a `*)` branch whose comment states the exact hazard — *"Anything else — including a network failure — must not be read as 'not published'"* — and that reasoning is right. But `set -euo pipefail` is on at `:28`, so `code=$(curl …)` exiting 35 killed the script **before** the `case` ran: the run died on a bare exit code with no message, and the branch written to handle precisely this could never fire. **A guard downstream of an aborting command is not a guard.**
>
> The probe is an idempotent `GET`, so `--retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 2 --max-time 30` cannot change what an answer means — the only thing retried is the question. Curl's exit status is captured with `|| status=$?` rather than `if ! curl`, because inside an `if !` branch `$?` is the negation's status and the whole point is to report *which* failure it was; a persistent outage now exits 1 naming the crate, the version and the curl code.
>
> ***Both directions demonstrated, because a retry that hides a real outage would be worse than the flake.*** The hardened script's real dry run probes all three crates clean and exits 0. The failure path was exercised against a closed port: four attempts (one plus three retries), `status` captured as curl's genuine **7** rather than 0, the `::error::` line printed with crate and version, script exit 1. `a gate that cries wolf is a gate somebody disables` — the same value M-304's row records — with the sibling clause that a gate which cannot say why is one nobody reads.
>
> ***Not a version bump and not a release.*** `publish.sh` uploads only when a manifest version is absent from crates.io, so this changes what an ordinary push *reports*, never what it publishes.

| ☑ | **D-021** | S | R-061 |
> **DONE 2026-08-26 — an index-out-of-bounds panic in `marching_cubes`, in release, on an ordinary trilinear cell (✗50 / M-373).** Found by R-061's harness before P-63 measured anything: an exhaustive sweep over all 2^18 sign patterns of a 3 x 3 x 2 block with magnitudes in general position reached `mod.rs:514` with `count == 24` on a `[[u8; 3]; MAX_PATCH_TRIANGLES]`. Not an `Error` and not a hole — a panic.
>
> ***Two bounds for one quantity, and the derived one was on the inside.*** `fan_tunnel` buffers its own output in `[[u8; 3]; 40]` and its body says where 40 comes from, so the function could never overflow itself. The **caller's** array was sized by `MAX_PATCH_TRIANGLES = 24` — a sampled maximum of 22 over 400,000 random cells, plus two for margin — and the caller receives every triangle the function emits. The reproducer is pattern `0x06b4a` cell 0, sign byte `0x96`: inside corners 1, 2, 4, 7, which is Marching Cubes **case 13**, and it emits **26**. Two over. The margin was the whole safety argument and it was two triangles wide.
>
> ***The fix is the derivation, written once, and the second literal deleted.*** `MAX_PATCH_TRIANGLES` is `40` and now carries `12 x 3 + 4` rather than a number: at most 3 triangles per ring edge, ring lengths summing to at most 12 because a cell has 12 cut edges, plus a 4-triangle closure when a single twelve-vertex ring leaves the hexagon open. **`fan_tunnel`'s buffer uses the same constant**, because raising 24 to 40 while leaving a second literal in place rebuilds the same defect one release later. B-006/B-007's rule in a third place, and the aggravating detail is that the derivation already existed eleven lines from the array that was too small.
>
> ***The existing test was never wrong; it was answering a different question.*** `the_worst_case_tunnel_triangle_count_is_pinned` still reads 22 over its 400,000 random cells and still passes. It pins what a **sample** reaches. Nothing pinned what the **construction** can reach, which is what a buffer has to be sized by. The counterexample is pinned as its own fixture with the eight corner values verbatim and unrounded, because the count depends on where the body saddles fall.
>
> ***Verification.*** `preflight --full` all green at **710** lib tests, one more than before — the new fixture. **No golden hash moves and none should**: the constant sizes a stack array and does not change an emitted triangle, so all 216 are unchanged.

Judged went **16,768 -> 19,415 of 19,415**, and the 2,647 missing were every exactly-zero-error crossing, concentrated in `box_exact` (0 of 1,350) and `csg_difference` (219 of 1,386) - a bias in the direction that flatters the bound.
>
> ***Two more controls.*** `two_sum`'s exactness is **asserted in `i128`** on six adversarial pairs, because the denominator term otherwise rests on a six-line function copied into a bench. And a sabotage arm requires a bound ten times too small to produce violations on the same data.
>
> ***One supporting change, a clean cutover:*** `cube::edge_offset` becomes `pub` and is re-exported through `marching_cubes::table` beside `is_inside`. `P-61` made it *the* definition of where a crossing is; anything measuring a crossing must ask the same question of the same expression, and a second copy of a one-line formula is the drift `x39` cost 216 golden hashes to find.

| ☑ | **D-024** | S | — |
> **DONE 2026-08-27 — a GPU test asserted a property of the *adapter*, and `0.0.10`'s own arithmetic change made it false on Metal. It failed CI on the release push, which skipped `publish to crates.io`.** `every_gpu_vertex_is_a_cpu_vertex_to_within_one_ulp`, `crates/isomesh-gpu/src/marching_cubes/tests.rs`.
>
> ***What broke, and it is `P-61` succeeding rather than failing.*** The test's contract is *"every GPU vertex is within one ULP of a CPU vertex"* — `strangers == 0` — and that held on both platforms. Beside it sat `assert!(within > 0, "every vertex agreed exactly -- this adapter does not contract")`, whose stated reason was that a zero there would mean the bound was being checked over an empty set. That reasoning is wrong twice: the bound is asserted over the **emitted vertices**, not over `within`, and *"this adapter contracts a multiply-add"* is a fact about the driver that this crate neither controls nor promises.
>
> ***The measurement, which is the finding.*** Same 33³ sphere, same 6,936 vertices, `strangers = 0` on both: **RTX 3090 / Vulkan 6,632 bit-exact and 304 within 1 ULP** (`M-142` measured 6,507 / 429 under the old parameter form), **Apple / Metal 6,936 and 0**. `P-61`'s centred offset has *fewer multiply-adds to contract*, so it reduced the divergence on one adapter and removed it on the other. `M-142`'s *"6% of vertices"* is amended to say it is that adapter's number.
>
> ***The fix is the guard the bound actually needs, not the guard that was there.*** Both directional counts are gone; what is asserted is `strangers == 0`, a non-empty population on both sides, and `exact + within + strangers == positions.len()` — complete accounting. A formula error needs no help from `exact > 0`: a wrong expression moves a vertex far further than one ULP and lands in `strangers`.
>
> ***Both replacements were shown failing before being left passing.*** Dropping a classification branch → *"every emitted vertex must be classified exactly once, left: 304, right: 6936"*. Widening the neighbourhood probe to ±3 ULP → *"96 gpu vertices are more than one ULP from any cpu vertex"*.
>
> ***The generalisable lesson, and it is why this got a ticket rather than a quiet edit.*** A non-vacuity guard must assert that the **population** is non-empty, never that the population is **distributed** a particular way. `within > 0` and `exact > 0` are distribution claims wearing a non-vacuity guard's clothes, and the arithmetic they described was changed by an experiment two phases later. `M-44`'s rule is *a zero that could not have been non-zero is not a measurement*; its converse is not *a count must be non-zero in every bucket*.
>
> ***Cost.*** One CI run on the release commit: `test (macos-latest)` red, so `publish to crates.io` was skipped by `needs:`. `deploy to github pages` is independent and succeeded, so the site went live at `0.0.10`'s content before the crates did.

Both arms are proved to be looking at the same scene, because a gather ratio is worthless otherwise — one liveness vector, one direction set, `hit_agree_frac` **0.9777–0.9921** (asserted > 0.8) and `hit_median_delta_cells` **0.0287–0.0778** — so the mesh is not fast because it misses; it hits *more* often.
>
> ***The vacuity control and C3 are the same instrument read on two arms, and the control arm's merge count differs by exactly one component.*** `Repair::merges` is the number of **pre-existing** components the newly-air blob touched, so 1 is an ordinary widening, 0 is an isolated bubble that *adds* a component, and only `>= 2` is `M-311`'s join. Measured: **`merges` = 2 exactly on all 36 breakthrough rows**, `air_components_before → after` always a drop of exactly one (2 → 1 or 3 → 2), `pocket_connected_after` **true**; **`merges` = 1 exactly on all 36 control rows**, components unchanged (2 → 2 or 3 → 3), pocket still sealed. The arms are *chosen* by the union-find rather than checked afterwards — 64 breakthrough candidates accepted only on `merges >= 2 && components() < before && connected`, 288 control candidates accepted only on `merges == 1 && components() == before && !connected` — each search has its own `expect`, and **the control's came back empty twice and halted the first two runs**. So neither number is a zero that could not have been non-zero: the same instrument reads 1 on one arm and 2 on the other arm of the same pair, and a control reading 2 would not have been a control at all. On that footing C3 HELD on **36 of 36** pairs, ratio **1.2500–2.5333**, median **1.8947**, with the volume match an integer identity rather than an approximation — `dug_samples` is **171 on every row of both arms**, so the effect is pure topology. The probe gap is **86–211** at `s = 2` and **8–23** at `s = 4`. **C3's weak spot is stated rather than smoothed**: at `s = 8` the "strictly more" is **5 against 4** on all 12 pairs, at a spacing where the dilated support holds 0.5586–0.7051 probes and `probes_in_support_actual` is literally **0** — which is also why `c1_holds` reads false on all 24 `s = 8` rows, and that false says the lattice is too coarse to answer, not that the invalidation is wide.
>
> ***Four fixture defects, three caught by the harness's own controls and one by review.*** (1) The first fixture inset the sealing block 6.25 cells on every face, which put 22.6% of the world inside it and cut the air labyrinth into interleaved fragments; the control-arm search reported **0 of 159 candidate digs usable** and the run stopped. At `BLOCK_INSET` = 2.25, **64 of 64** breakthrough directions merge and **112** control candidates widen exactly one component — **the fix was the block, not the level set**, and the canonical `iso = 0` is kept. (2) `brush_support_cells` was `value_changed_cells` first and the no-clipping control refused it: `max(f, −sphere)` moves the *value* wherever `−sphere > f`, and `f` reaches −30 deep inside the sealed block, so a brush's value support is tens of cells across and **grows with the world** — a quantity that grows with world size cannot be the denominator of a clause about world-proportionality, and it would have hidden exactly the effect C1b was looking for. It is now `M-314`'s `output_changed_cells`, local to the ball by construction; `value_changed_cells_in_region` is still emitted as a **window** on an unbounded set and reads **625** against an output-changed 286 on every control row and **547** against 359–361 on every breakthrough row — larger where the other is smaller, which is the clearest possible proof they are different quantities. (3) The arm predicates misread `merges`, asking `>= 1` on the breakthrough arm and `== 0` on the control — "any dig" against "a dig that opens a new bubble", both wrong; reading `grow_from` rather than guessing is what fixed it. (4) **Caught by review, not by a control:** C2's same-scene columns (`hit_frac_field`, `hit_frac_mesh`, `hit_agree_frac`, `hit_median_delta_cells`) were added *after* the first successful run, because a ratio between two arms is worthless if the arms are not tracing the same geometry and nothing in the harness had asserted that they were.

The clipper carries each piece as vertices tagged with the sorted ids of their three defining planes and takes two vertices to be adjacent exactly when they share two planes, which is sound for a **simple** polytope and false for the non-simple ones an oblique 14-plane set makes: four planes through a point put three tagged vertices on one plane pair, two of them at the same position, and both chords to the third produce the same crossing vertex. Rather than report a piece count from an arrangement that does not tile its own cube, the arm was removed — **every row in `p-84.csv` is `dop_dirs = 6`**. **A clipper that derives vertices from plane triples rather than from edges is the fix, and that is a design change**, the one piece of work this row files against the construction itself. Five further defects were caught the same way, by this harness's controls rather than by review: aliased cube-face plane ids bred false edges until one piece reached **8.4 million vertices in a single 268 MB allocation** and the process was OOM-killed (`degenerate_vertices == 0`); a split half pruned with the wrong orientation left one cell's sole surviving leaf at 8.6e-5 against 1.5625e-2, caught by the same volume closure at a relative error of exactly **1.0**; a compound that did not carry each cell's surface plane pruned every surface-bounded piece to nothing (`fragments > 0`); the canonical sort ran *after* the centroid and volume sums it was supposed to canonicalise, manufacturing two order dependencies in front of the exact question C2 asks; and `simplicity_scan` showed the 6-DOP arm is not immune either — `coincident_plane_pairs = 3` in 3 of the 182 cut cells, `nonsimple_points = 36`, `max_planes_at_a_point = 4`, and those 36 points are precisely the 36 zero-width leaves the sliver filter was silently absorbing while `degenerate_vertices` and `singular_triples` both read clean, because **neither counter can see two distinct ids naming the same plane.**
>
> ***Stop tracking the convex-decomposition literature.*** `M-297` holds: VisACD (`arXiv:2604.04244`) is a **GPU** method averaging 16.97 s per model against CoACD's 36.31 s — four orders of magnitude off a frame budget. Thirteen years after Müller, nobody has improved on *preserving* convexity instead of *recovering* it, and `A-027` proposes his construction without citing him. **This row is the last time that literature needs a look**, and C1's real content is that the 2013 result reproduces with three to four orders of headroom against its own bar on 2026 hardware — a reason the design is not the risk, not a reason to spend a phase on it.
>

> ***The reason to prefer this over Recast is that nothing in it ever sees a triangle.*** Recast rebuilds a tile by voxelising collision geometry, so this game would voxelise a mesh it generated from voxels; the whole structure here is derived from the sign bits and the active-cell bitmap, and a `MIXED` unit cell — the surface passes through it — *is* the obstacle, which is the paper's *"cells containing obstacles are split"* taken to the leaf, where there is nothing left to split. That is why nothing in the repair chain is indexed by world size: an edit flips bits in the brush box, re-derives `AIR`/`SOLID`/`MIXED` for every cell of every dirty 4³ chunk, walks the pyramid bottom-up **over its own ancestors only** — `nodes_reevaluated` is **714–1,767** for eleven edits and the world contributes only `octree_depth`, which is 5, 6, 7, 8 — and rebuilds leaves under the topmost changed nodes plus the free-leaf pool of every region that lost a member (`max_pool_leaves`, the largest single-edit pool, is **145–263**). >
> ***C1 registers the single edit, and the eleven-edit reading is reported rather than gated because a wall clock moved 1.67× on the identical binary.*** The registration says *"the local repair after P-72's eleven-edit dig trace costs under 2 ms"* and does not say whether the subject is one edit or the trace; the two readings differ by **8.19–9.82×** on the `p72_dig` arm. Under the eleven-edits-in-one-frame reading `trace_total_ms` exceeds 2 ms on exactly four rows (both fields at 128³ and 256³ on `p72_dig`) at **2.3611–2.5396 ms**, 1.18–1.27× the bar, and holds on all eight `breakthrough` rows at 0.8793–1.1847. The superseded run, taken while ~25 sibling agents compiled, read **2.88–4.25 ms** on those same four rows: the verdict did not flip and **the margin did** — and the margin is now smaller than the spread the identical binary showed on this very column between two runs: whole-trace worst 4.2487 → **2.5396 ms** is a **1.67×** move on the same binary and the same fixture, and one element of `rebuild_over_repair` moved 30%. So *"the eleven-edit dig does not fit a 2 ms frame budget"* is withdrawn as a conclusion under `✗24`, and the claim is re-grounded on integers: the trace reclassifies **12,288–23,040** cells, `nav_dirty_chunks × 64` exactly on all 16 rows, over **192–386** dirty 4³ chunks, and that chunk set is **0.7567–0.9326** of the `mesh_dirty_chunks` `mark_edit` hands the *mesher* for the same eleven edits — **never above 1, on every row**. Whatever a frame costs, this repair is a strict fraction of a stage the crate already pays for, and that is the only form of the sentence that survives a re-run. The reading that matters for a consumer is the total, and `word_ops_total` = **24** = `word_op_bar` = **24** — `word_ops_plane_build` = 12, four `dx = 0` planes free and four `dx = 1` planes at `(lo >> 1) | (hi << 63)`, three operations each, which is `dual.rs:395`'s `inside_word_shifted` verbatim. **The registration's bar had no slack in it.** One extra operation anywhere in the plane build falsifies C1 under the strict reading, and `c1_holds_with_plane_build` is carried as its own column so a later reader cannot quietly take the loose one.
