> ***C1 is the whole row and it was decided by arithmetic that predated the harness.*** `c1_holds` is false on 24 of 24 and no denominator rescues it: `offset_share` (`cycles_offset` over `cycles_extract_mc`) runs **0.000328** at `fbm_terrain` 129³ to **0.009714** at `sphere` 33³, `offset_share_dc` ≤ **0.005629**, `offset_share_instructions` ≤ **0.008045**, `offset_share_scan_only` ≤ **0.006004**, and zero rows clear 0.05. So an offset stage reduced to *zero cost* moves marching-cubes extraction by `1/(1 − 0.009714)` = **1.0098×** and dual-contouring extraction by `1/(1 − 0.005629)` = **1.0057×** — one part in a hundred and one part in two hundred. `falsified_by` named this outcome in words (*"Amdahl-dead the way `✗51` was, and closes the row before C2 is built"*), and three priors already pointed at it: `M-135`'s contour stage at 29% of the pipeline, `✗54`'s GPU scan at **4.37%** of `gpu_total_ms` — already under the bar on the other path — and `P-121`'s `(cycles_emit_prepare + cycles_emit_walk) / cycles_total` at **0.0800**, a strict *superset* of the offset work. The measurement lands an order of magnitude below even that superset. Nothing about the registration was wrong; it was right for the reason it said, and it was measured anyway because a share inherited from a neighbouring definition is exactly how `✗51` happened.
>
> ***The falsification is conservative in the mechanism's favour, and it still cannot reach one percent.*** The harness keys its dense slot table by **cell** and pays `slot_table_bytes` **131,072 / 1,048,576 / 8,388,608**; the crate keys the same object by `(sample, axis)` at `marching_cubes/mod.rs:250-251` and pays `crate_edge_table_bytes` **431,244 / 3,295,500 / 25,760,268** — **3.07× to 3.29× larger** at every resolution. The numerator the share is taken against is therefore about a third of the one the shipped extractor actually clears and refills on every extract, and the share tops out at 0.97% regardless. Building the bitmap is deliberately excluded from the numerator, because `P-121` already assigned the bit-packing and the fused `any & !all` word test to `classify`, and counting them here would inflate C1 with sign tests a rank directory does not remove. A reader who rejects the memset entirely scores the clause on `offset_share_scan_only` and gets a smaller number, not a larger one.
>
> ***C2 and C3 held, so what the row bought is a structure proved correct and proved cheap.*** `overhead_fraction` is **0.032227** on all 24 rows — `directory_bytes` **264 / 1,056 / 8,448** over `bitmap_bytes` **8,192 / 32,768 / 262,144**, and the 1,056-over-32,768 row is precisely the registration's *"about 1.1 KiB on a 64³ chunk's 32 KiB bitmap"* reproduced rather than restated. The O(1) half is scored as a count and never as a clock: `max_words_scanned_rank` = **7** on all 24 rows and does not move with resolution, while `max_words_scanned_scan` is **1,023 / 4,090 / 32,746**. C3's equality is total rather than sampled — `slots_equal` = `active_cells` on every row from **512** (`thin_plate` 33³) to **118,885** (`noise_cavity` 129³), and `rank_equal_all_bits` = `cells_checked` on every row, so the agreement covers all **65,536 / 262,144 / 2,097,152** bit positions and not merely the active ones, with `directory_total_equals_popcount` true 24/24 and `pad_bits_set` 0 on 24/24. `R-112` consumes this directory as the middle phase of its count/scan/scatter, and it is available to consume because C2 and C3 held.
>
> ***The honest comparand is the shipped sequential walk, the directory loses to it, and that is the finding rather than an embarrassment.*** The shipped path never asks a random slot question — it walks cells in order with a running counter — and that costs `instructions_per_query_sequential` **0.259–2.553** (`ns_per_query_sequential` 0.0139–0.2712) against the rank query's `instructions_per_query_rank` **126.754–131.868**, so the directory is **51.7× to 496.1× dearer per query** than the pass it would replace. What it buys is **random access, not throughput**, which is the one property `R-112` needed — and `R-112` failed anyway: its rank arm came in **2.2× to 8.6× slower** (`speedup` 0.116376–0.461247 against a 1.25 bar) because the scan the directory removes is only **3.7% to 15.9%** of that pass, a scan-free ceiling of **1.1890×**. `M-280`'s hazard sits in this file in plain view: the `ghz` column spans **1.3077** (`torus` 129³) to **4.1834** (`sphere` 33³) across the 24 rows of a **single** run, so `query_ratio_ns` **35.346–1,470.878** carries no verdict at all and the instruction form is the one that decides. `instructions_per_query_rank` is flat in resolution; `instructions_per_query_scan` **4,776.389–166,672.475** is not, which is the O(1) claim in the only unit that can hold it.
>
> ***No source change landed, no landing ticket is earned, and the vacuity control is what makes C3 admissible.*** `crates/isomesh/src/` was read-only for the whole of Phase 25 apart from the twenty registrations, so nothing here is a new baseline and no golden hash moved — stated explicitly because `V-45`'s failure mode is a landing that was never registered. **No landing ticket is filed, and `offset_share` ≤ 0.009714 is the number that decides it**: a mechanism that wins its own microbenchmark and moves under 1% of an extraction is the `✗51`/`R-114` shape, and refusing to land it is the result. The controls fired in both directions: `short_directory_mismatches` — the identical query answered by a directory built deliberately one level short — reads **47,104 to 1,651,200** and is never zero on any row, so C3's equality is between two computations that *could* have disagreed rather than two names for one (`M-44`), and `bitmap_matches_scalar` true on 24 of 24 pins the ranked bitmap to the scalar predicate before any rank is taken. `target_feature_popcnt` is false on all 24 rows and no verdict is contingent on it: `count_ones_per_query_rank` is **4.566** flat against `count_ones_per_query_scan` **507.836 / 2,069.836 / 16,253.836**, so hardware popcount would move both arms the same way, and the offset stage — `trailing_zeros` and `word &= word − 1` — issues none at all, leaving the gating clause popcount-independent.

The module doc's SHARE section refuses the inheritance in advance — *"this harness measures the share itself and does not inherit that"* — and puts `cycles_per_cell_shipped_extraction` (**40.9027 to 1088.4135** across the 32 rows) beside `cycles_per_cell_flat` (**0.026149 to 0.395882**) on every row, so the share is a division of two numbers taken in the same binary rather than a citation. `M-337` is not wrong; it measured a *stage against itself*, and the premise that converted it into "large enough to matter" was never a measurement at all. The lesson transfers to any registration that cites a prior stage figure as licence: a stage ratio is not a share, and the share must be a column.
>
> ***The win does not generalise, and the boundary is `active_fraction`.*** `ratio` = `ns_per_cell_flat / ns_per_cell_hier` spans **0.9049** to **2.5678**, and it is **below 1 on 8 of 32 rows** — every `gyroid` and every `noise_cavity` row, at both depths. Two-level readings: `gyroid` 129³ **0.9087** at `active_fraction` **0.04128456**, `noise_cavity` 129³ **0.9137** at **0.05668879**, `gyroid` 65³ **0.9889** at **0.08175659**, `noise_cavity` 65³ **0.9937** at **0.10824203**. `breakeven_traversals` reads **`inf`** on all 8 — no number of traversals amortises a build whose per-traversal saving is negative — against **1.367 to 5.351** on the 24 winners, which is the honest single-shot caveat: the summary must be shared across at least two traversals before it is ahead. At 4.1% and 5.7% active the second level is a net cost, and `ghz` 4.1653–4.1875 with `clock_ratio_hier_over_flat` 0.9976–1.0035 across all 32 rows says no reading here is a clock artefact. Per `M-280` the nanosecond form is still not the gate; `ratio_instructions` puts the same eight rows at 0.9931–1.0296, seven of the eight at or above parity, so the loss is thin in instructions and real in cycles.
>
> ***C2's 4,096 was a best case reported as a mean, and 16 of the 21 failures were decided by arithmetic before the harness existed.*** `cells_skipped_per_test` is `cells_skipped_total / summary_words_tested`. At one level the divisor *is* `level_1_words` = `level_0_words / 64` — 64 at 65³, 512 at 129³ — so the quotient is at most `cells / level_1_words` = 262,144/64 = 2,097,152/512 = **exactly 4,096**, and that ceiling is attained only by a bitmap with **zero active cells**. All **16 `levels` = 1 rows** therefore fail, at 3,072.000–4,064.000; the sparsest, `thin_plate` 129³, reads **4,064.000** = 4,096 × (2,080,768/2,097,152) — a clause registered as *"≥ 4,096"* over a population with 8,192 active cells cannot fire upward. At two levels the divisor is `level_2_words + level_1_words_nonzero`, so 4,096 is reachable only where a level-2 word is *wholly* empty; the registered figure is the fan-out of one zero top-level bit (`cells_per_top_level_zero_bit` = **4096.0** on 15 of 16 two-level rows), a **best case**, while the column reports the **mean over every summary word tested**. `active_fraction` separates the outcome without a residual: every cleared row sits at **0.00390625–0.02294159**, every failing two-level row at **0.03209305–0.10824203**. The full span is 1,820.000 (`gyroid` 65³, one level) to 15,299.765 (`thin_plate` 129³, two levels). The one-level rows carry the same column and the same bar deliberately, so the discrimination is visible in the data rather than argued in prose.
>
> ***One fixture limit the module doc predicted in advance rather than discovered.*** `fbm_terrain` 65³ at two levels is the single row with `top_level_fanout_verified` **false** and `zero_top_level_bits` **0**, and it is the only row where adding the second level makes the mechanism *worse* on its own C2 column: `cells_skipped_per_test` **falls from 3,513.000 at one level to 3,458.954 at two**. The cause is geometric and was written down before the run: at 65³ one level-1 word spans a whole `z` slice, a heightfield crosses every slice, so `level_1_words_nonzero` is **64 of 64** — the second level contributes a divisor and removes nothing. Its skipping is still real, via empty level-0 words inside tested level-1 words, which is why the row is a reading and not a defect. The dense-level-1 pattern is the same one that sinks the two-level C2 elsewhere: `gyroid` 129³ 398 of 512, `noise_cavity` 129³ 336 of 512, `gyroid` 65³ 56 of 64, `noise_cavity` 65³ 48 of 64.
>
> ***The vacuity control fired on all 32 rows rather than the one the registration demanded, and the gap it opens is this row's real lesson.*** The registered control asks only that `words_tested_hier` be **strictly less** than `words_tested_flat` **on at least one row**; it holds on **32 of 32**, with `word_ratio` spanning **1.7504** (`gyroid` 65³, one level) to **83.5918** (`thin_plate` 129³, two levels), and `cells_skipped_per_test` non-zero on 32 of 32 (minimum 1,820.000). Then the sparsest row tests **97** summary words against the flat arm's **4,096** — a **42.2×** reduction in words tested — and buys **1.612×** of wall clock. That gap between a 42.2× reduction in tests and a 1.6× reduction in time is the clearest statement in the file: the flat walk's cost is not in the word tests, so no amount of further summarising reaches it. The hypothesis's own first sentence is verified rather than assumed — `level_1_size_ratio` and `level_2_size_ratio` read **64.0000** on 32 of 32 and `summary_overhead_fraction` is **0.015869** (= 65/4096) on every row. **No source change landed.** `crates/isomesh/src/**` was read-only for the phase apart from the twenty registrations; the entire hierarchy is bench-local, mirroring `row_stride`, `build_inside_bits`, `inside_word`, `active_word` and `cell_mask` line for line, so there is nothing here that could have landed unregistered — `V-45`'s failure mode is structurally absent. All eleven read identically on both targets: the comparison is a source-level both-ways evaluation, so it is a property of the arithmetic and not of a backend, and `reachable` is true on 32 of 34 rows — false only on the two bench-local `control::searched_separator` rows, whose triple is searched for rather than harvested.

> ***The two figures near 2⁶² are sign-crossings, which is a predicate flip rather than a rounding wobble.*** On `marching_cubes::corner_position` and `dual::place_vertices` — the two sites that convert a grid index to a world coordinate, and between them the entire coordinate-generation path — `unfused_value` is exactly `0.00000000000000000e0` (`unfused_result` `0x0000000000000000`) and `fused_value` is **`-4.44089209850062616e-16`** (`fused_result` `0xbcc0000000000000`). `ulp_difference` is an integer bit distance, so stepping across the sign bit costs about 2⁶² of it; `relative_difference` reads **1.0** and `worst_case_cancels` **true** on both. The statement that matters is that a coordinate landing *exactly on* a lattice plane stops doing so, on 83,936 and 152,064 inputs respectively, and `golden.rs:35-38` is already on record that the fixture hashes raw IEEE bits precisely so a sign flip on a zero coordinate is the class of change it catches. `vec3::cross` is the third of that family — exact `0` becoming `2.74129141882754686e-17`, `relative_difference` 1.0 — without crossing the sign.

Any future `-C target-feature=+fma` build, any `-ffast-math` equivalent, or one hand-written `mul_add` at any of the eleven named sites moves golden hashes — two of them by turning an exact zero into a signed epsilon — and `P-61` already proved the 216-hash gate can fire by moving 135 of them.

Three source comments asserted the safe reading — `real.rs:45` (`mul_add` deliberately absent), `fields/noise.rs:17` (*"nothing here asks for one"*) and `predicates.rs:28` (which says the same and adds *"but this is asserted rather than assumed"*) — and all three were statements about what the source *requests*, none about what the arithmetic is *sensitive to*. That last one is `predicates.rs:28`'s own stated worry, and it reads zero — the worry belongs to a different rewrite than the one it names — and `on_extraction_path` is **false** there, because the extractors never call the module. Fixed at `0b51cd8` — the commit that took eight errors out of four never-linted wave-3 harnesses — and the census is now **seven extra columns**. The decisive one is `buckets_of_three_or_more_spanning_chunks`, the only bucket kind whose *member count* chunk append order can change: first fit elects a different **number** of representatives only out of a chain of three or more, and only a bucket straddling a chunk boundary has its member order moved by a concatenating `MeshBuffer::append`. It reads **0 on 16 of 16**. The supporting counts. **12 of 16** rows have no bucket at all (`buckets_of_two_or_more` = 0). The two `torus` rows have **4** buckets of two or more, all **4** of them spanning chunks (`buckets_spanning_chunks` = 4), but `largest_bucket` = **2**, and a pair elects one representative in either order. `noise_cavity` holds the only chains — `buckets_of_three_or_more` **1** under `dual_contouring` and **2** under `manifold_dual_contouring`, each equal to `p9_published_buckets_of_three_or_more`, `largest_bucket` **3** — and `buckets_spanning_chunks` is **0** on both, so those chains sit inside one chunk and the append never reorders them. Meanwhile `chunk_orders_distinct` = **8 of 8** proves the perturbation was genuinely applied and the zero is not a harness that forgot to shuffle. C1's vacuity is a property of the fixture's geometry, decided before a single permutation ran, and it is now **measured** rather than inferred — the census is a function of the identity-order mesh alone.

> ***Two readings a scanner will trip over, both by construction and neither a defect.*** `cycles_solve` is **0.0 on 36 rows and all 36 are `marching_cubes`** — the registration puts `solve` on the dual path only, so a zero there is the decomposition working, and C1's other half (*"any stage reading zero on a fixture where it must run"*) is asserted per row over the stages that must run, `cycles_sample` ≥ **184439.1** and `cycles_classify` ≥ **453230.3** on every row of the file. And `field` carries **nine** distinct values where the crate has eight reference fields: the ninth is **`sphere_surface_free`**, C3's registered surface-free control — the canonical sphere sampled a long way from itself (`experiment_p40.rs:84-93`, already scored on by `M-337` and `✗28`) — with `active_cells` = `vertices` = `triangles` = **0 on all 8 of its rows**. Its exclusion from C2's maximum is load-bearing, not tidiness: the file's overall `integer_share` maximum is **0.759249** on `sphere_surface_free 65³ f32 dual_contouring`, *higher* than the gate number, because on a field with no surface integer work is trivially most of what remains. Quoting that cell as the gate would have inflated Group A's ceiling off a field no consumer meshes. All three registered vacuity controls fired and one of them fired both ways: `instructions_emit` falls to **36.0** on the surface-free dual rows against a file maximum of **8596148.0** while `cycles_classify` there reads **4477616.1** and **4713889.3**, **96.3%** and **97.1%** of `sphere`'s — the same instrument reading a near-zero and a near-full number side by side, which is `M-44` demonstrated rather than asserted.
>
> ***No source change landed, and this row earns no landing ticket because there is nothing to land.*** `crates/isomesh/src/` was read-only for the whole phase apart from the twenty `Preregistration` entries; the five-stage decomposition is a **bench-local mirror** of the extractor, every formula called from the public surface (`table::{CASES, EDGE_AXIS, EDGE_CORNERS, edge_offset, is_inside}`, `HermiteCell::from_corners`, `solve::solve_with`) and the seven private helpers copied verbatim rather than made `pub`. The mirror's licence to be read at all is `M-279`'s: `mesh_identical_to_shipped` is **true on 72 of 72**, positions, normals and indices compared as bit patterns in creation order. `agreement_ratio` spans **0.7798 – 1.0279**, so the mirror is up to **22% cheaper** than the shipped extractor on the cheapest Marching Cubes rows while emitting its mesh bit for bit — every share in this file is therefore a share of the *mirror's* cycle profile, disclosed here rather than assumed away, and that is the one caveat a future reader must carry forward rather than rediscover. There is no mechanism, no microbenchmark win and no share to weigh: **the durable output of `R-121` is the number 0.724533 and the three tickets it kept alive**, and `V-45`'s failure mode — a landing that was never registered — cannot apply to a row whose registration forbids landing anything. `docs/experiments.md`'s Phase 25 scorecard reads this row as the phase's denominator, not as a candidate.

| ☑ | **R-122** | S | — |
> **DONE 2026-08-29 — 💥 ✗96 / M-435 / P-122: C1 FALSIFIED on 0 of 16 rows with `branch_miss_ratio` spanning 1.001214–1.983313 — the split doubles mispredictions at worst and reduces them nowhere — C2 HELD at a worst `instruction_ratio` of 0.970606 against a 1.10 bar, i.e. *below* unity on every row, and C3 HELD bit for bit on 32 of 32. Stream VByte's layout transfers and its promise does not: the second traversal of the cell space costs one extra misprediction per innermost-loop exit, and the shipped shape had only 0.008–0.251 per cell to give up.** `docs/experiments/p-122.csv`, 32 rows, 55 columns, sixteen (field, resolution) pairs — eight fields × {65³, 129³} — each emitted twice, once as `arm = single_stream` and once as `arm = split_stream`.
>
> ***C1 is falsified in the direction that closes the question rather than deferring it: not marginal, worse everywhere.*** `rows_reducing_branch_misses` = **0** of `rows_total` = **16** on all 32 rows, and `branch_miss_ratio` runs from **1.001214** (`gyroid` 65³, = `best_branch_miss_ratio`) to **1.983313** (`thin_plate` 129³, = `worst_branch_miss_ratio`); `branch_misses_per_cell_single` **0.008008–0.250699** against `branch_misses_per_cell_split` **0.015883–0.251252**, with `c1_holds` and `c1_holds_all_rows` both `false` on 32 of 32. The distribution is the interesting part: the ratio is worst exactly where the field is compact and the misprediction rate already near zero — `thin_plate` 129³ at 1.983313 with an `active_fraction` of 0.003906, `box_exact` 129³ 1.784051, `csg_difference` 129³ 1.718677 — and nearest 1.000 where there was most to remove, `noise_cavity` 65³ 1.002204 at 0.250699 misses per cell and `gyroid` 65³ 1.001214 at 0.230113. **The mechanism removes nothing anywhere, and where the headroom was largest it removed least.** That is the opposite shape from a mechanism that works and is being diluted.
>
> ***C2 held below 1, which the registration did not budget for, and the harness closed the one alternative explanation that would have credited the win to somebody else.*** `worst_instruction_ratio` = **0.970606**, per-row `instruction_ratio` **0.853904** (`thin_plate` 129³) to **0.970606** (`noise_cavity` 65³) — the split is **2.9% to 14.6% cheaper** in instructions, `instructions_per_cell_single` **119.6579–306.5750** against `instructions_per_cell_split` **102.1763–297.5637**. The registration bounded a cost it expected to pay and the cost came back negative; the module doc had predicted the direction, because the control pass is a straight loop the optimiser can transform in ways it cannot transform the fused body, and that win *is* the mechanism rather than a confound. The confound it could have been is `P-121`'s 15–24% corner-gather saving, and three integer columns rule it out: `gather_calls_single` = `cells` (**262,144** at 65³, **2,097,152** at 129³), `gather_calls_split` = `cells + emitting_cells` (**264,192–2,216,037**), and `gather_calls_ratio` **1.003906–1.108242**, **strictly above 1 on all sixteen comparisons** — the split arm gathers eight corner values *more* often, not less, because its payload pass re-reads them rather than carrying an `[R; 8]` per cell across the pass boundary. A mechanism cannot be credited with a saving on a stage it runs more times. `instruction_ratio_rep_spread` = **0.000000** on 32 of 32 demonstrates `M-279`'s determinism instead of asserting it, which is why the instruction form of the clause is the one that carries a verdict at all.
>
> ***The instrument's own honesty note is this row's best content: one of sixteen verdicts is decided by which arm ran second.*** The arms alternate order by repetition parity, and `branch_miss_ratio_single_first` / `branch_miss_ratio_split_first` are the medians *within each ordering*. On **`gyroid` 65³** they straddle unity — **1.002346** single-first against **0.999613** split-first — so on that row whether the split reduced mispredictions is a fact about cache and predictor inheritance, not about the layout. The aggravating detail is which row it is: `gyroid` 65³ carries `branch_miss_ratio` = **1.001214**, the **most favourable firm ratio of all sixteen**. Had C1's verdict rested on its best row it would have rested on the one row that cannot bear it — it does not, 0 of 16 is the verdict, but the fragility is a column rather than a footnote, and the printed summary counts it (*"rows whose verdict flips with the ordering: 1 of 16"*). `branch_miss_ratio_rep_best` dips below 1 on four 65³ rows — `csg_difference` **0.745632**, `gyroid` **0.989480**, `fbm_terrain` **0.999837**, `noise_cavity` **0.980458** — against `branch_miss_ratio_rep_worst` of **1.066253–2.249289** on the same rows, so a single lucky repetition is not a reduction either. This is `M-280` at row granularity: the governed-clock caveat applied to a counter ratio, per row, with the two orderings kept as data so a later reader cannot promote a fragile row to a firm one.
>
> ***The popcount baseline is unusually complete for a Phase 25 row, and it was established by reading machine code rather than by reading the call graph correctly.*** `target_feature_popcnt` = **`false`** on all 32 rows, so `u64::count_ones` lowers to the ~12-instruction SWAR sequence in this build — and **neither arm touches the quantity**: `count_ones_calls_per_cell_single` and `count_ones_calls_per_cell_split` are both **0.0 on 32 of 32**. The control stream is one case **byte** per cell, `control_stream_bytes` = `cells` exactly (**256 KiB** at 65³, **2 MiB** at 129³), scanned through a `payload_length_table_bytes` = **256** length table — Stream VByte's shape is a byte stream, so there is no bitmap, no rank, no select and no word-population fold to pay for. And the harness `objdump -d`s its own binary: **0** `popcnt` instructions and **0** occurrences of **`0x3333333333333333`**, the SWAR magic constant, while the sibling row that found the build fact reports **18** of that constant in its own binary — so the grep is shown to discriminate rather than merely to return zero. **No verdict on this row is contingent on the popcount lowering and both surviving clauses are invariant to `-C target-cpu=native`.**
>
> ***The vacuity control fired, and the headroom it revealed is precisely why C1 failed.*** `branch_misses_per_cell_single` is non-zero on all 16 single-stream rows, **0.008008–0.250699**, asserted per row rather than merely recorded, because a ratio taken against a floor of zero is not a measurement. But the floor is *low*: at `thin_plate` 129³ the shipped fused loop mispredicts **0.008008 times per cell** — **under one misprediction per 125 cells** — so C1's entire reachable share on that row was eight thousandths of a branch, and the split added **0.007875** more instead of removing any. `M-44`'s rule is satisfied in both directions here: the zero could have been non-zero, it was not, and the non-zero it was is small enough to explain the outcome on its own. There was very little to remove and the split added rather than removed.
>
> ***The mechanism is attributed rather than guessed, and the attribution is honest about where it stops.*** `extra_branch_misses_per_pass` is the signed difference, **+73.2 to +16,619.6**, and `extra_branch_misses_per_x_row` divides it by `x_rows`, the innermost-loop exits in one traversal (**4,096** at 65³, **16,384** at 129³). The split traverses the cell space twice, so it must pay `x_rows` extra loop exits — and at 129³ that column reads **0.9615–1.0144 on all eight rows**, which assigns essentially the *whole* difference to the second traversal's loop exits. At 65³ it reads **0.0179–0.8690**, so **the accounting is complete only at the larger grid** and the 65³ excess is partly unexplained; say both, because a column near 1.0 on half the file is an attribution and not a law. **No landing ticket, and none is owed.** C1 is a per-cell counter ratio rather than a fraction of extraction time and C2 is a cost bound, so no time claim exists to price and `✗51`'s share bar does not apply — and **whether a misprediction reduction would have been worth anything in wall time is a question this row deliberately does not answer**, which is moot since there was no reduction. Stream VByte's published **4 billion integers per second on a 3.4 GHz Haswell** is the `_mm_shuffle_epi8` SIMD path; the registration says so in its own hypothesis text, there is no SIMD arm here, and nothing was scored against that figure. **No source change landed**: both arms are bench-local, `crates/isomesh/src/` was read-only for the phase apart from the twenty registrations, and C3 held bit for bit on **32 of 32** on both readings — `mesh_identical` (`split == single`) and `mesh_identical_to_shipped` (`single == MarchingCubes::extract`, positions, normals and indices compared as bit patterns in creation order) — so no golden hash moved and there was nothing for `V-45` to catch.
